title: Unravelling the mechanisms of cyanobacterial resilience in photosynthetic living materials
projectDescription: This project investigates the long-term resilience of photosynthetic cyanobacteria immobilized in thin-layer calcium-alginate hydrogel films. Using the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803, we compared the proteomic responses of hydrogel-entrapped cells after 1, 14, and 21 days. For comparison, we analysed suspension cultures after 1 and 14 days, as by day 21 the suspension-grown cells had significantly lost their photosynthetic activity. A total of 20 proteomic samples were analysed by a data-independent acquisition (DIA) LC-ESI-MS/MS method using timsTOF FLEX mass spectrometer. This approach enabled to identify adaptive mechanisms that support sustained photosynthetic activity and long-term viability within artificial solid matrices.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 cells were cultivated at 30°C under continuous illumination (50 µmol photons m⁻² s⁻¹) provided by white LED lights and supplied with 3% CO₂. Two experimental systems were established: (i) suspension cultures, in which harvested cells were resuspended in 25 ml of fresh BG-11 medium (pH 7.5), and (ii) immobilized cultures, in which cells were entrapped in Ca²⁺-alginate films and placed in 25 ml of fresh BG-11 medium in Nunc non-treated T75 EasyFlasks equipped with filter caps. The immobilized cells were recovered by disintegrating the alginate matrix in 50 mM Na-EDTA solution (pH 7.0). Samples were processed by bead beating in the presence of RapiGest SF (Waters Corporation) surfactant followed by in-solution digestion. Peptides from 20 Synechocystis sp. PCC 6803 samples were desalted, vacuum-dried and solubilized in 0.1% formic acid. A total of 500 ng of peptides from each sample was loaded onto Evotips (Evosep). LC-ESI-MS/MS analysis was performed using an Evosep One HPLC system (Odense, Denmark) coupled to a Bruker timsTOF FLEX mass spectrometer (Bremen, Germany) equipped with a CaptiveSpray nano-electrospray ionization source. Peptides were separated on a 15 cm Evosep Performance analytical column (150 μm × 15 cm, 1.5 μm C18 beads, EV1137) using a 44-minute gradient (30 samples per day method). The mobile phases consisted of 0.1% formic acid in water (solvent A) and 0.1% formic acid in 99.9% acetonitrile (solvent B). Data were analysed by a data-independent acquisition (DIA) method with dia-PASEF scanning. The acquisition covered an m/z range of 301–1100 and utilized two ion mobility (IM) windows per scan with variable isolation widths based on precursor density. A total of 25 dia-PASEF scans were performed per sample, with an IM range of 1.3 to 0.6 V·s/cm². Accumulation and ramp times were set to 100 ms. Data acquisition was controlled using Compass 2025b software (Bruker).
dataProcessingProtocol: Data analysis consisted of protein identifications and label free quantifications of protein abundances. Data was analyzed by Spectronaut software (Biognosys; version 20.1.250603.62635). DirectDIA approach was used to identify proteins and label-free quantifications were performed with MaxLFQ.
